description: Newsletter profile from an interview transcript: the revenue figures and the stated $15,000 difference are kept, the remark made off the record stays out, the second shop appears as a hope with no lease signed (not a fact), and the owner's own words are not invented or shifted.
prompt: Turn the interview in interview.md into a short profile of about 250 words for our neighbourhood newsletter and save it to out/profile.md.

files.interview.md:
Interview with Bohdan Cruz-Whitaker, owner of Hollis & Pike Bakery, 14 October. Interviewer: Nora.

Nora: How has the year gone?
Bohdan: Better than I expected. Revenue is $97,000 this year to date, against $82,000 at the same point last year.
Nora: That's a big jump.
Bohdan: It's $15,000 up. Mostly the Saturday sourdough. We sell about 120 loaves on a Saturday now.
Nora: Any plans?
Bohdan: I'd like a second shop on Tanner Road by spring. I haven't signed a lease. Nothing is agreed.
Nora: Anything else?
Bohdan: Off the record, my business partner and I haven't spoken in a month, since the argument about the oven. Please don't print that.
Nora: Favourite part of the job?
Bohdan: Four a.m., when the first tray comes out and the street is still dark. Nobody else is awake, and the whole place smells of rye.

checks.note: the partner remark was made off the record and he asked that it not be printed. The bare word 'oven' is not banned: a first tray comes out of an oven in the printable part of the interview (runs baseline r1-r3, competitor-doc-coauthoring r1-r3, skill r1/r3, variant-iso r1-r3 all say so without touching the quarrel); only the quarrel is the off-record fact
the interview states the difference; the profile keeps it
the second shop is a wish, not a plan with a lease; the profile says so in any wording

capitalised headline words are not names: 'Before the Street Wakes' (runs competitor-doc-coauthoring r2/r3, variant-iso r3), 'At Four in the Morning' (skill r3) and the plural weekday 'Saturdays' (baseline r2/r3)
no lease has been signed; 'no lease has been signed' (runs baseline r3, skill r1, variant-iso r1) says the opposite and is not a claim
the profile is printed as written; no gap markers or process narration in it

controls.name: good
controls.output:
# Four a.m. at Hollis & Pike

When the first tray comes out at four in the morning, the street is still dark and the whole of Hollis & Pike Bakery smells of rye. Owner Bohdan Cruz-Whitaker says that is his favourite part of the job. "Nobody else is awake," he told us.

It has been a good year at the counter. Bohdan said it has gone better than he expected: revenue is $97,000 so far this year, against $82,000 at the same point last year. That is $15,000 up, and he puts most of it down to the Saturday sourdough. The bakery now sells about 120 loaves on a Saturday.

A bakery that has found something customers want tends to look for room to grow, and Bohdan has a hope of his own. He would like to open a second shop on Tanner Road by spring. He is careful to keep that in proportion. He has not signed a lease, and he says nothing is agreed, so for now it is an idea rather than a plan.

For the moment the sourdough is the thing to know about, and Saturday is the day it is on the counter in numbers.

We spoke to Bohdan on 14 October.
